You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From eaa2f87c6b840b83827c40db6eb8481689570259 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2017 13:30:30 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] x86/ldt: Fix off by one in get_segment_base()

ldt->entries[] is allocated in alloc_ldt_struct().  It has
ldt->nr_entries elements and ldt->nr_entries is capped at LDT_ENTRIES.
So if "idx" is == ldt->nr_entries then we're reading beyond the end of
the buffer.  It seems duplicative to have two limit checks when one
would work just as well so I removed the check against LDT_ENTRIES.

The gdt_page.gdt[] array has GDT_ENTRIES entries.

Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Acked-by: Andy Lutomirski <luto@kernel.org>
Cc: Alexander Shishkin <alexander.shishkin@linux.intel.com>
Cc: Arnaldo Carvalho de Melo <acme@kernel.org>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: kernel-janitors@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: d07bdfd322d3 ("perf/x86: Fix USER/KERNEL tagging of samples properly")
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20170818102516.gqwm4xdvvuvjw5ho@mwanda
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/x86/events/core.c b/arch/x86/events/core.c
index af12e294caed..939050169d12 100644
--- a/arch/x86/events/core.c
+++ b/arch/x86/events/core.c
@@ -2335,12 +2335,9 @@ static unsigned long get_segment_base(unsigned int segment)
 #ifdef CONFIG_MODIFY_LDT_SYSCALL
 		struct ldt_struct *ldt;
 
-		if (idx > LDT_ENTRIES)
-			return 0;
-
 		/* IRQs are off, so this synchronizes with smp_store_release */
 		ldt = lockless_dereference(current->active_mm->context.ldt);
-		if (!ldt || idx > ldt->nr_entries)
+		if (!ldt || idx >= ldt->nr_entries)
 			return 0;
 
 		desc = &ldt->entries[idx];
@@ -2348,7 +2345,7 @@ static unsigned long get_segment_base(unsigned int segment)
 		return 0;
 #endif
 	} else {
-		if (idx > GDT_ENTRIES)
+		if (idx >= GDT_ENTRIES)
 			return 0;
 
 		desc = raw_cpu_ptr(gdt_page.gdt) + idx;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/events/core.c`**
   - Removed the check `if (idx > LDT_ENTRIES)` which was redundant since `idx` should not exceed the number of entries in the LDT.
   - Changed the condition `if (idx > ldt->nr_entries)` to `if (idx >= ldt->nr_entries)` to prevent reading beyond the allocated entries in the LDT.
   - Similarly, modified the condition `if (idx > GDT_ENTRIES)` to `if (idx >= GDT_ENTRIES)` to ensure that the index does not exceed the number of entries in the GDT.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the `arch/x86/events/core.c` file are related to improving the safety of index checks when accessing the LDT and GDT structures. By consolidating the checks to use `>=` instead of `>`, the patch ensures that the code does not attempt to access an out-of-bounds index, which could lead to undefined behavior or crashes. The removal of the redundant check against `LDT_ENTRIES` simplifies the logic, making it clearer and more efficient while maintaining the integrity of the data access. Overall, these changes enhance the robustness of the segment base retrieval function by preventing off-by-one errors.

Here is the commit message:
x86/ldt: Fix off by one in get_segment_base()

ldt->entries[] is allocated in alloc_ldt_struct().  It has
ldt->nr_entries elements and ldt->nr_entries is capped at LDT_ENTRIES.
So if "idx" is == ldt->nr_entries then we're reading beyond the end of
the buffer.  It seems duplicative to have two limit checks when one
would work just as well so I removed the check against LDT_ENTRIES.

The gdt_page.gdt[] array has GDT_ENTRIES entries.

Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Acked-by: Andy Lutomirski <luto@kernel.org>
Cc: Alexander Shishkin <alexander.shishkin@linux.intel.com>
Cc: Arnaldo Carvalho de Melo <acme@kernel.org>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: kernel-janitors@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: d07bdfd322d3 ("perf/x86: Fix USER/KERNEL tagging of samples properly")
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20170818102516.gqwm4xdvvuvjw5ho@mwanda
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by an off-by-one error in the index checks when accessing the entries of the LDT (Local Descriptor Table) and GDT (Global Descriptor Table). Specifically, the original checks allowed for the possibility of accessing an index equal to the number of entries, which is out of bounds, leading to potential memory access violations. The redundant check against `LDT_ENTRIES` was unnecessary since `ldt->nr_entries` already caps the valid index range.

Here is the patch:
 
 static unsigned long get_segment_base(unsigned int segment)
 {
 	struct desc_struct *desc;
 	unsigned int idx = segment >> 3;
 
 	if ((segment & SEGMENT_TI_MASK) == SEGMENT_LDT) {
 #ifdef CONFIG_MODIFY_LDT_SYSCALL
 		struct ldt_struct *ldt;
 
-		if (idx > LDT_ENTRIES)
-			return 0;
-
 		/* IRQs are off, so this synchronizes with smp_store_release */
 		ldt = lockless_dereference(current->active_mm->context.ldt);
-		if (!ldt || idx > ldt->nr_entries)
+		if (!ldt || idx >= ldt->nr_entries)
 			return 0;
 
 		desc = &ldt->entries[idx];
 #else
 		return 0;
 #endif
 	} else {
-		if (idx > GDT_ENTRIES)
+		if (idx >= GDT_ENTRIES)
 			return 0;
 
 		desc = raw_cpu_ptr(gdt_page.gdt) + idx;
 	}
 
 	return get_desc_base(desc);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c

```
```c

```
```c

```
Reason:
The bug occurs due to an off-by-one error in the index checks when accessing the entries of the LDT and GDT. The condition `idx > LDT_ENTRIES` and `idx > ldt->nr_entries` allow for the possibility of accessing an index equal to the number of entries, which is out of bounds. This can lead to memory access violations. The check against `LDT_ENTRIES` is redundant since `ldt->nr_entries` already limits the valid index range.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (idx >= ldt->nr_entries)
```
```c
if (idx >= GDT_ENTRIES)
```
Reason:
The fix changes the conditions to `idx >= ldt->nr_entries` and `idx >= GDT_ENTRIES`, which correctly prevent accessing an index that is equal to the number of entries. This ensures that any access to the entries array remains within valid bounds, thus preventing potential memory access violations.
